coordinate_frame: Workstation metres, +X east, +Y north, +Z up; radians; wxyz quaternions
objective: Unlock the spring dial code by finding and simultaneously holding one correct nonzero input. Minimize execution time and valid attempts using only historical BEST feedback; preserve real grasps and required airborne support.
rules: The face has0,1,2,3,4,5 at60-degree intervals. Each private password digit is1..5;0 is an invalid initial position. Clockwise labels4 and5 may be reached as-120 and-60degrees; +180 and-180 are the same mark3.

BEST starts at0 and shows the largest correct-count achieved by any one complete valid input in this episode. It is not the current correct-count. An unchanged record can mean equal or worse; never combine per-dial results from different attempts.

READY is grey when the current input is invalid, amber while qualifying and green after every dial is within4degrees of a nonzero mark, actually grasped, and stable for0.25seconds. Green means a valid input, not a correct password.

The BEST digit is bright only when READY is green. Otherwise its retained value stays visible in dim grey-brown, including while the amber lamp is qualifying. Brightness does not change the record or disclose current correctness.

Only a complete valid input updates BEST. Off-mark, zero or lost grasp makes READY invalid while BEST remains. New stable configurations are evaluated automatically, including intermediate configurations during movement; bind a record change to an actually observed configuration, not an assumed target.

L2/L3 require a separate robot to hold each blue handle with the whole module at least20mm clear of external supports. Maintain that support during red operation. A crank grip moves around the axle and may require coordinated translation.
Unlock occurs only when all digits of one simultaneous valid input are correct. Success latches, while physical springs and support remain active. Inputs and actuation choices are Agent decisions.
Only robot actuators and real contacts may affect the live world. Use RGB and permitted robot feedback; hidden passwords, per-dial correctness and live object truth are not policy inputs.

completion.success_semantics: Unlock once with a simultaneous valid correct input; success remains latched after later dial changes.

mechanism.feedback_stability: same nonzero 4-degree detent band throughout the dwell; in-band vibration allowed

feedback.display_brightness: Bright only when READY is green; otherwise dim but readable
feedback.readiness: Grey invalid, amber qualifying, green ready; readiness is not password correctness

policy: Selected timestamped RGB including BEST and READY

process_requirements.grasp_feedback_scope: Width/drive inference; confirm object retention and support with permitted observations

description: Operate spring dials and movable modules with paired support, and interpret BEST/READY feedback as evidence.

# Dial

The robot `ready` tool reports robot capabilities; it is unrelated to the dial
apparatus READY indicator. Before judging table-edge or ring-cutout clearance,
read the geometry reference in `static_workstation`, and use `camera_calibration`
to relate views to the common frame.

## Feedback as evidence

Bind each BEST/READY reading to the timestamped RGB configuration that produced
it, keeping intended settings separate from disk positions you can verify. A
commanded wrist angle describes the tool; the dial's angle belongs to the movable
white disk's frame, which you update after slip or reorientation. An unchanged
BEST does not tell you whether the current input is equal or worse, or which dial
is correct: keep that uncertainty in your note and choose the next experiment from
the observed configuration. Passing through an intermediate stable configuration
can create a valid trial before the commanded target is reached. A contradiction
can come from your assumptions or from execution or observation error.

## Support and manipulation

Derive red operation and blue support from reach, grasp access and commitments;
nominal robot groups describe layout. For a movable module, establish and observe
independent blue-handle support before red contact, and keep the module clear of
external supports. Choose support contact and bearing direction for load moments;
support must resist the partner's reaction forces while preserving approach,
articulation and withdrawal. After support loss, stop the affected operation and
reassess the geometry before re-establishing it.

For an eccentric crank, plan the translating grip point and tool orientation
together in the apparatus frame, and compare approaches with their next
operations: continued turning, partner support, opening and withdrawal. Observe
at useful milestones, since small contact errors change that frame. Keep useful
held settings while other work progresses, counting spring load, drift and the
cost of an occupied gripper.

## Recovery

After a failed move or opening, use the original action's terminal feedback and
selected RGB to distinguish an admission failure, a settled failure and an unknown
outcome. Confirm actual opening and separation before retreating or changing a
supporting grasp; keep sustained support while it is needed.
